newsitem.title: USA: U.S. high-yield bonds gain, Nextel active.
newsitem.headline: U.S. high-yield bonds gain, Nextel active.

text.p: U.S. high-yield bonds were lifted 1/4 to 1/2 point in the broad market on Tuesday with bonds of Nextel Communications Inc outperforming the pack, dealers said.
Investment grade bond spreads, meanwhile, were unchanged as the U.S. Treasury market ticked higher. Traders said new issues, including a $750 million Philip Morris Cos deal, were the primary focus,
Back in high-yields, Nextel debt rose more than one point after the company announced it added 72,300 subscribers in the fourth quarter and launched its nationwide wireless network.
The service, known as Nextel National Network, carries no roaming fees -- which are charged by most other providers of cellular and wireless communications.
Nextel 9-3/4 percent debt of 2004 was quoted at 69-3/4 bid late on Tuesday compared to a 68-1/2 to 69 market on Monday.
Elsewhere, Penn Traffic Co's 9-5/8 percent debt traded as low as 38-1/8 before closing at 40-1/2 bid, 42 offer.

Traders said lower-than-expected December same-store sales started the recent selloff. Selling was dominated by one primary account along with others dumping the debt based on double-digit losses over the course of 1996, one trader said.

Elsewhere, high-yields tagged along with stronger U.S. Treasuries with most issues registering 1/4 to 1/2 point gains. Along with Nextel, Flagstar Cos Inc senior debt outperformed and closed up more than one point to 93-1/2.

Turning to investment grade trade, prices also rose in sympathy with Treasuries but spreads were mostly unchanged as some big new supply began to hit the market. Dealers reported moderate volume from investors seeking to capitalize on higher rates spawned by the recent backup in Treasuries.

Apache Corp debt tightened by two to three basis points based on rating upgrade by Standard & Poor's rating agency late on Monday, one trader said. Senior unsecured debt was raised to BBB-plus and subordinated debt was raised to BBB.

Topping the new issue slate, Philip Morris Cos issued $750 million in A2/single-A rated 30-year bonds as 7-3/4s to yield 7.824 percent or 101 basis points over the Treasury long bond. The deal, which was increased in size by $250 million, was said to sell briskly to primarily institutional accounts.
Merrill Lynch & Co Inc was lead manager on the deal.

Also on Tuesday, JP Morgan & Co Inc issued $300 million 10-year Aa3/AA rated 10-year notes as 6-7/8s to yield 6.992 percent or 47 basis points over the Treasury curve via a JP Morgan Securities syndicate.
Huntington National Bank issued $100 million A1/single-A rated short-term bank notes at par to yield 6.15 percent or 17 basis points over Treasuries.

Trust preferred issues included $350 million capital securities from Philips 66 Cap II via Merrill Lynch. The Baa1/BBB-plus rated 40-year securities were given an eight percent coupon and priced to yield 8.005 percent or 119 basis points over the Treasury long bond.

In the Treasury market, the benchmark 30-year bond closed a full point higher at 96-17/32 to yield 6.77 percent. A mild gain of 0.3 percent in the overall U.S. Consumer Price Index and a 0.1 percent increase in the core CPI sparked the upmove on Tuesday morning, Treasury market analysts said.
